SELECT c.category, c.id AS course_id, COUNT(e.id) AS enrollments
FROM courses c
JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.category, c.id
HAVING COUNT(e.id) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(e2.id) AS cnt
    FROM courses c2
    JOIN enrollments e2 ON e2.course_id = c2.id
    WHERE c2.category = c.category
    GROUP BY c2.id
  )
)
ORDER BY c.category;

SELECT c.category, c.id AS course_id, COUNT(e.id) AS enrollments
FROM courses c
JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id

HAVING COUNT(e.id) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(e2.id) AS cnt
    FROM courses c2
    JOIN enrollments e2 ON e2.course_id = c2.id
    WHERE c2.category = c.category
    GROUP BY c2.id
  )
)
ORDER BY c.category;

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT c.category, c.id AS course_id, COUNT(e.id) AS cnt
  FROM courses c
  JOIN enrollments e ON e.course_id = c.id
  GROUP BY c.category, c.id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT category, course_id, cnt,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY cnt DESC, course_id) AS rn
  FROM counts
)
SELECT category, course_id, cnt
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY category;
